entities.summary: The hadith is a collection of sayings and teachings attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (570–632 CE), which have shaped Islamic law and practice. These sayings, known as ahadith, were often passed down orally before being written down, and they provide valuable insights into the Prophet's life, teachings, and the social context in which he lived. The hadith has played a significant role in the development of Islamic jurisprudence, particularly in the areas of law, worship, and ethics. Shia Muslims also consider the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet's family, to be equally authoritative. The hadith has been a subject of scholarly debate and analysis, with many Islamic scholars and jurists contributing to the collection and interpretation of these sayings. The hadith has had a profound impact on Islamic culture and society, shaping the practices and traditions of millions of Muslims around the world. As a result, the hadith remains a vital component of Islamic scholarship and practice, continuing to inform and guide Muslims to this day.
